title: Does subtracting ten and adding one always work?
description: A child subtracts nine by taking away ten and adding one back, and the video asks if this always gives the right answer. It then finds similar strategies for taking away eight and adding nine.
teaching_notes: Let the child try first, then compare. One idea: taking away too much and adding the extra back leaves the answer unchanged. Ask the child to find another number that works the same way.

video_script.why: The child sees that taking away too much and adding the extra back leaves the answer right, as in taking away a difference.
video_script.substitution: The same strategy works with other numbers: round to ten, then put the extra back.
video_script.anchor: thirty six on a number line, with a jump back of ten and a small jump forward of one
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, it always works, since minus nine is minus ten plus one.

final_answer.value: (a) Yes, always, since −9 = −10 + 1 (b) for example −8 = −10 + 2 and +9 = +10 − 1
final_answer.spoken: yes, always, since minus nine is minus ten plus one; for example minus eight is minus ten plus two, and plus nine is plus ten minus one

names.{{NAME_1}}: everyday child, not a character of the book

maths_rules: taking away 10 takes away 1 too many, so adding 1 back puts it right: -9 = -10 + 1, for any number
video_script.design: One idea: take away or add a round number, then put the difference back. The number line stays in the anchor band; the working band shows each strategy. No hard clear.

<bookmark mark='m3'/>Thirty six plus ten minus one is forty five, which is thirty six plus nine.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Every pair matches.
